answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. This works because the originality bar tightens as more low-quality answers appear, raising the per-alias cost of a coordinated fake campaign. So the design does not rely on catching every cheat — it makes cheating unprofitable, which is a far more stable defense than any whitelist ever could be. Consider a zenith as the anchor of the cost.
